en: Established by authority.
Admitted to the ministry of the church.

ex.en: God has ordained that all men shall die.
ex.ja: 神は人間はみな死ぬものと定めた。

note.ja: ordain（聖職に任命する）+ -ed。ラテン語 ordinare（整える）、ordo（順序）。order と同じ ord。

en: The complete loss of voluntary control of part of a living body, such as one or more limbs.
A state of being unable to act.

paralysis.ety: Borrowed from Latin paralysis, from Ancient Greek παράλυσις (parálusis, “palsy”), from παραλύω (paralúō, “to disable on one side”). By surface analysis, para- + -lysis. Doublet of palsy.

ex.en: The accident left him with paralysis in his legs.
ex.ja: その事故で彼は脚が麻痺した。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 paralysis（体の片側の弛緩）から。para（そばに）+ lyein（ほどく）。「麻痺」。analysis と同じ lyein。

en: In a patient manner.

patiently.ety:
Etymology tree
English patient
Proto-Indo-European *leyg-der.
Proto-Germanic *līkąder.
Proto-Germanic *-līkaz
Proto-Germanic *-ê
Proto-Germanic *-līkê
Proto-West Germanic *-līkē
Old English -līċe
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English patiently
From patient + -ly.

ex.en: I listen patiently, but without interest.
ex.ja: 根気強く聞いてはいるけど、興味はない。

ex.en: He was angry, but he listened to me patiently.
ex.ja: 彼は怒っていたが、私のいうことをがまんして聞いた。

ex.en: He was patiently digging for facts.
ex.ja: 彼はこつこつ事実を調べていた。

note.ja: patient（忍耐強い）+ -ly。「辛抱強く」。

en: The soft foot of a mammal or other animal, generally a quadruped, that has claws or nails; comparable to a human hand or foot.
Of an animal, to dig through (something, such as a garbage can) with paws.
Of an animal, to draw the forefoot along the ground; to beat or scrape with the forefoot.

paw.ety:
From Middle English pawe, from Old French poue, poe, from Vulgar Latin *pauta. Further origin unknown, perhaps from Frankish *pōta, from Frankish *pōtōn (“to put, stick, plant”), from Proto-Germanic *putōną, whence also Old English potian (“to push”), pȳtan (“to put out, poke out”). See more at put. Doublet of pote, put, and putt.
Cognate with Dutch poot, poten (“to plant”), Low German Pote, German Pfote, Icelandic pota (“to stick”).

ex.en: Get your dirty paws off me.
ex.ja: 私に触らないで。

ex.en: I saw a dog with one paw bandaged.
ex.ja: 私は片足に包帯を巻いた犬を見た。

ex.en: The cat likes fish, but doesn't like getting its paws wet.
ex.ja: その猫は魚が好きなんだけど、足が濡れるのが嫌なのよ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 poue（足）から。「（動物の）足」。

en: A person who plays the piano, particularly with skill or as part of an orchestra.
A spy using radio or wireless telegraphy to keep in touch with headquarters during the Second World War.

pianist.ety: From French pianiste, from Italian pianista. Analyzable as piano + -ist.

ex.en: The pianist played a trick on the audience.
ex.ja: ピアニストは聴衆をだました。

ex.en: As a pianist, he is far above me.
ex.ja: ピアニストとしては彼は私よりはるかに優れている。

ex.en: The girl grew up to be a pianist.
ex.ja: その少女は成長してピアニストになった。

note.ja: piano + -ist。piano は pianoforte（弱く強く弾ける楽器）の短縮。

en: Any traveler.
An early American settler.
To make a pilgrimage

pilgrim.ety:
Inherited from Middle English pilegrim, from Old English pilegrī̆m, from Old French pelegrin, from Latin peregrīnus (“foreigner”). Doublet of peregrine.
The change of /r…r/ to /l…r/ is an effect of dissimilation in early Romance; compare Italian pellegrino.

ex.en: I decided to go away with the pilgrims.
ex.ja: 遍路さんたちと一緒に去る事に決めた。

ex.en: The party of pilgrims started for Shikoku.
ex.ja: お遍路さんの一行は四国に向かった。

note.ja: ラテン語 peregrinus（よそ者）から。per + ager（土地）。「土地を越えて旅する人」→「巡礼者」。

en: A dummy medicine containing no active ingredients; an inert treatment.
The vespers sung in the office for the dead.

placebo.ety: Inherited from Middle English placebo, borrowed from Latin placēbō (“I will please”), the first-person singular future active indicative of placeō (“to please”).

ex.en: Some patients felt better after taking a placebo.
ex.ja: 偽薬を飲んだあとで具合がよくなった患者もいた。

note.ja: ラテン語で「私は喜ばせよう」。placere（喜ばせる）。患者を安心させるための薬 →「偽薬」。please と同じ。

en: To delay or put off an event, appointment, etc.

postpone.ety: From Latin postpōnō (“to put after; to postpone”) from post (“after”) + pōnō (“to put; to place”), compare forestall.

ex.en: I've decided to postpone my trip to Boston.
ex.ja: ボストンへの旅行は延期することにしたよ。

ex.en: I've decided to postpone my trip to Australia.
ex.ja: オーストラリア旅行は延期することにしたよ。

ex.en: Why don't we postpone this until next week?
ex.ja: これ、来週に延期しない？

note.ja: post（後に）+ pon（置く）+ e。後ろに置く →「延期する」。

en: In a progressive manner.
As part of a progression.

progressively.ety:
Etymology tree
English progressive
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English progressively
From progressive + -ly.

ex.en: The situation is growing progressively worse.
ex.ja: 状況はどんどん悪化してます。

note.ja: progressive + -ly。「次第に」。

en: To provide an impetus for motion or physical action; to cause to move in a certain direction; to drive or push forward.
To provide an impetus for nonphysical change; to cause to arrive to a certain situation or result.

propel.ety: From Middle English propellen (“drive out, expel”), from Latin propellō, from pro- (“forward”) and pellō (“to push, to move”).

ex.en: The engine propels the boat forward.
ex.ja: エンジンがボートを前に進める。

note.ja: pro（前へ）+ pellere（押す）。「前へ押す」→「推進する」。propeller、compel と同じ pel。

en: A narrow shallow boat, square at both ends, traditionally propelled by a pole.
To propel a punt or similar craft by means of a pole.
Of a fish, to walk along the seafloor using its fins as limbs.

punt.ety: From Old English punt, from Latin pontō (“Gaulish flat-bottomed boat, pontoon”), from pons (“bridge”); readopted from Middle Low German punte (“ferry boat”) or Middle Dutch ponte (“ferry boat”) of the same origin.

ex.en: The player decided to punt the ball.
ex.ja: その選手はボールをパントすることにした。

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。ボールを地面に落とす前に「蹴る」こと。（英）小舟の punt は別語。

en: The act, process, or state of reinforcing or being reinforced.
A thing that reinforces.

reinforcement.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Italic *wre-
Latin re-der.
Old French re-bor.
Middle English re-
English re-
English inforce
English reinforce
Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥
Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥tom
Proto-Italic *-mentom
Latin -mentum
Old French -mentbor.
Middle English -ment
English -ment
English reinforcement
From reinforce + -ment.

ex.en: The general asked for reinforcements.
ex.ja: 将軍は増援を要請した。

note.ja: reinforce（強化する）+ -ment。「強化・増援」。

en: The act or an instance of repeating or being repeated.
The act of performing a single, controlled exercise motion. A group of repetitions is a set.
To petition again.

repetition.ety: Borrowed from Latin repetitionem (accusative singular of repetitio; cf. French répétition). Doublet of repetitio. By surface analysis, repeat + -ition.

ex.en: Repetition plays an important role in language study.
ex.ja: 言葉の学習には繰り返しが必要です。

ex.en: Repetition helps you remember something.
ex.ja: 繰り返すことが物事を覚えるのに役に立つ。

ex.en: Every successful repetition spoke favorably for the quality of the first test.
ex.ja: うまく行われれば何回実験を繰り返しても、最初の実験の質が十分保証されるのだった。

note.ja: re（再び）+ pet（求める）+ ition。何度も求めること →「繰り返し・反復」。repeat（繰り返す）。

ja: 抑制する（restraining order：接近禁止命令）

en: The act by which someone or something is restrained.

ex.en: She is restraining the boy.
ex.ja: 彼女は男の子を引き止める。

note.ja: restrain（抑える）+ -ing。restraining order（接近禁止命令）。restraint と同じ。

en: Of, relating to, or contemplating the past.
Looking backwards.
An exhibition of works from an extended period of an artist's activity.

retrospective.ety: From retrospect + -ive. From Latin retrōspectus, perfect passive participle of retrōspiciō (“to look back at”).

ex.en: The museum is holding a retrospective of her work.
ex.ja: その美術館は彼女の作品の回顧展を開いている。

note.ja: retro（後ろへ）+ spectare（見る）+ -ive。「振り返って見る」→「回顧的な・回顧展」。spectator と同じ spec。

en: The quality or state of being righteous.
Holiness; conformity of life to the divine law.

righteousness.ety: Corruption of earlier rightwiseness, from Middle English rightwisnes, from Old English rihtwīsnes (“justice”). By surface analysis, righteous + -ness.

ex.en: Education is the path to happiness, peace, righteousness, and success.
ex.ja: 教育は幸福と平和と正義と、そして勝利の道なのであります。

note.ja: righteous（正しい）+ -ness。「正義」。

en: To wash (something) quickly using water and no soap.
To remove soap from (something) using water.
The action of rinsing.
A liquid used to rinse, now particularly a hair dye.

rinse.ety:
From Middle English rinsen, rincen, rencen (“to rinse”), from Old French rincier, reinser, Old Northern French raïncer (“to rinse, cleanse”). Of contested origin. Possibly from Old Norse hreinsa, from Proto-Germanic *hrainisōną (“to clean, purify”), from Proto-Indo-European *krey- (“to separate, divide”). Alternatively from a dissimilation of Old French recincier, from Latin recentare (“to make fresh”).
Cognate with French rincer. From the Germanic verb are Danish rense, Norwegian rense, Swedish rensa (all “to clean”), Old High German reinisōn (“to clean, purify, atone”). It is related to Germ

ex.en: I have to rinse out my mouth.
ex.ja: 口をゆすがなくちゃ。

ex.en: I have to rinse my mouth out.
ex.ja: 口をゆすがなくちゃ。

ex.en: I need to rinse my mouth.
ex.ja: 口をゆすがなくちゃ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 rincer（すすぐ）から。「すすぐ」。

en: The part of the head where the hair grows from, or used to grow from.
A part of the skin of the head, with the hair attached, formerly cut or torn off from an enemy by warriors in some cultures as a token of…
To remove the scalp (part of the head from where the hair grows), by brutal act or accident.
To bet on opposing competitors so as to make a profit from the bookmaker.

scalp.ety: From Middle English scalp, skalp, scalpe (“crown of the head; skull”). Originally a northern word, and therefore probably from a North Germanic source, although the sense-development is unclear; compare Sylt North Frisian Skolp (“dandruff”), Old Norse skálpr (“sheath”), Old Swedish skalp, Dutch schelp (“shell”).

ex.en: My scalp is very itchy.
ex.ja: 頭皮がかゆいのです。

note.ja: 北欧語 skalpr（さや）から。「頭皮」。

en: One who shuts or closes something.
Each of a series of protective panels, usually wooden, placed over windows to block out the light.
To close shutters covering.
To close up (a building) for a prolonged period of inoccupancy.

ex.en: It's about time to replace these shutters.
ex.ja: この雨戸もそろそろ取り替え時ね。

ex.en: I've decided to replace the shutters.
ex.ja: 雨戸を取り替えることにしたんだ。

ex.en: I forgot to open the shutter.
ex.ja: シャッター開けるの忘れてた。

note.ja: shut（閉める）+ -er。「閉めるもの」→「よろい戸・シャッター」。

en: The full width of an open hand from the end of the thumb to the end of the little finger used as an informal unit of length.
Any of various traditional units of length approximating this distance, especially the English handspan of 9 inches forming ⅛ fathom and …
To extend across (a gap or space between two sides).
To cover or extend over (an area or distance).

span.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *(s)pend-der.
Proto-Germanic *spannō
Old English spann
Middle English spanne
English span
From Middle English spanne, from Old English spann, from Proto-Germanic *spannō (“span, handbreadth”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)pend- (“to stretch”).
Cognate with Dutch span, spanne, German Spanne. The sense “pair of horses” is probably from Old English ġespan, ġespann (“a joining; a fastening together; clasp; yoke”), from Proto-West Germanic [Term?]. Cognate with Dutch gespan, German Gespann.

ex.en: What is the average life span in Japan?
ex.ja: 日本での平均寿命はどれだけですか。

ex.en: The average life span of a dog is 10 years.
ex.ja: 犬の平均寿命は10年です。

ex.en: His life spanned nearly a century.
ex.ja: 彼の生涯はほぼ１世紀にわたった。

note.ja: 古英語 spann（手を広げた長さ）から。「範囲・期間」→「またがる」。

en: The house sparrow, Passer domesticus; a small bird with a short bill, and brown, white and gray feathers.
A member of the family Passeridae, comprising small Old World songbirds.

sparrow.ety:
From Middle English sparewe, sparowe, sparu, sparwe, spearewe, sperrewe, from Old English spearwa, from Proto-West Germanic *sparwō, from Proto-Germanic *sparwô, from Proto-Indo-European *spḗr (“sparrow”).
Cognates
Cognate with Yola sparrowe (“sparrow”), North Frisian sparag, spåri (“sparrow”), Saterland Frisian Spräie (“sparrow”), Alemannic German and Luxembourgish Spatz (“sparrow”), Dutch spreeuw (“starling”), German Spatz, Sperling (“sparrow”), Vilamovian śpielik, śpjelik, śpjeliḱ (“sparrow”), Yiddish שפּערל (shperl, “sparrow”), Danish and Norwegian Bokmål spurv (“sparrow”), Faroese spurvur

ex.en: Not a single sparrow was to be heard.
ex.ja: スズメの鳴き声一つしなかった。

ex.en: That bird is probably a sparrow.
ex.ja: あの鳥は、多分スズメだよ。

ex.en: A sparrow is very alert in its movements.
ex.ja: 雀は動作が非常にすばしこい。

note.ja: 古英語 spearwa から。「スズメ」。

en: To make an inference based on inconclusive evidence; to surmise or conjecture.
To make a risky trade in the hope of making a profit; to venture or gamble.

speculate.ety: Borrowed from Latin speculātus, perfect active participle of speculor (“to watch, observe, examine, spy”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from specula (“a watchtower”), ultimately from speciō (“to look at”).

ex.en: He has been speculating on his future.
ex.ja: 彼は自分の将来について思い巡らせていた。

ex.en: I am speculating that he may win the game.
ex.ja: 僕は彼が試合に勝つのではないかと推測している。

note.ja: ラテン語 speculari（見張る）から。specere（見る）。「よく考える」→「推測する」→ 先を見て「投機する」。spectacle と同じ spec。

en: Any member of species Spinacia oleracea of edible plants, or its leaves.
Any of numerous plants, or their leaves, which are used for greens in the same way Spinacia oleracea is or resemble it in some way.

spinach.ety: From Middle English spinach, from Anglo-Norman spinache, from Old French espinoche, from Old Occitan espinarc, from Arabic إِسْفَانَاخ (ʔisfānāḵ), from Classical Persian اسپناخ (ispanāx, ispināx).

ex.en: There are people who don't like spinach.
ex.ja: ほうれん草が嫌いな人もいる。

ex.en: It seems like you really hate spinach.
ex.ja: 本当にほうれん草が嫌いみたいね。

ex.en: Tom knows that I hate spinach.
ex.ja: トムはね、私がほうれん草大嫌いなこと知ってるよ。

note.ja: ペルシャ語 aspanākh から、アラビア語・ラテン語を経た語。「ホウレンソウ」。

en: Relatively short or low, and thick or broad.
Sitting on one's heels; sitting close to the ground; cowering or crouching.
A position assumed by bending deeply at the knees while resting on one's feet.
Any of various modes of callisthenic exercises performed by moving the body and bending at least one knee.
To bend deeply at the knees while resting on one's feet.
To exercise by bending deeply at the knees and then rising, while bearing weight across the shoulders or upper back.

From Middle English squatten, from Old French esquatir, escatir (“compress, press down, lay flat, crush”), from es- (“ex-”) + quatir (“pre

ex.en: Tom doesn't know squat about Mary.
ex.ja: トムはメアリーについて何も知らない。

ex.en: 300 squats a day? That's completely impossible!
ex.ja: 1日300回のスクワット？そんなの絶対無理！

ex.en: Seen at a distance, the rock looks like a squatting human figure.
ex.ja: 少し離れて見ると、その岩は人がしゃがんだ姿に見える。

note.ja: 古フランス語 esquatir（押しつぶす）から。「しゃがむ」→ 空き家に居座る →「不法占拠する」。

en: A heated bath-room or steam-room; also, a hot bath.
A dish cooked by stewing.
To cook (food) by slowly boiling or simmering.
To brew (tea) for too long, so that the flavour becomes too strong.

stew.ety: From Middle English stewe, stue, from Anglo-Norman estouve, Old French estuve (“bath, bathhouse”) (modern French étuve), from Medieval Latin stupha, of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Vulgar Latin *extufāre, from ex- + Ancient Greek τῦφος (tûphos, “smoke, steam”), from τύφω (túphō, “to smoke”). See also Italian stufare, Portuguese estufar. Compare also Old English stuf-bæþ (“a hot-air bath, vapour bath”); see stove.

ex.en: Could you give me a hand with this stew?
ex.ja: このシチューを作るの手伝ってくれないかしら。

ex.en: The stew was not half bad.
ex.ja: シチューは決して悪い味ではなかった。

ex.en: I will go to buy the meat for the stew.
ex.ja: シチューの為の肉を買いに行く。

note.ja: 古フランス語 estuver（湯気で温める）から。「とろとろ煮る」。stove と同系。

en: To heat (a substance) in a container so as to convert it into a gas which then condenses in solid form on cooler parts of the container; …
To raise (someone or an intangible thing) to a state of (especially moral or spiritual) excellence; to exalt.
Of an aspect of art or nature: causing awe or deep respect due to its beauty or magnificence; awe-inspiring, impressive.
Of flight: ascending, soaring.
An aspect of art or nature which causes awe or deep respect due to its beauty or magnificence; hence, the great beauty or magnificence of…
A style of language or writing which expresses opinions in a grand way.

sublime.ety:
PIE word
 *upó
Partly from the following:
* From Middle English sublimen, sublime, sublyme (“to exalt, extol, glorify, honour; (alchemy) to refine (a substance) by vaporizing in a closed container; to obtain (a substance) by cooling vapour obtained through sublimation; to extract (a pure substance) from a mixture by sublimation; to sublimate (a substance)”), from Middle French sublimer, Old French sublimer (“to exalt, glorify, honour; to refine (a substance) by vaporizing in a closed container; of a substance: to undergo sublimation”) (modern French sublimer), and from its etymon Latin sublīmā

ex.en: His death was a sublime self-sacrifice.
ex.ja: 彼の死は崇高な自己犠牲だった。

ex.en: It was sublime scenery.
ex.ja: それは崇高な光景であった。

note.ja: ラテン語 sublimis（高く掲げられた）から。sub（下から）+ limen（敷居・まぐさ）とされる。「崇高な」。

en: A heading below or after a title.
Textual versions of the dialogue in films (and similar media such as television or video games), usually displayed at the bottom of the s…
To create subtitles for the dialogue in a film.

From sub- + title.

ex.en: Tom watched a Japanese movie with French subtitles.
ex.ja: トムは、フランス語の字幕付きで日本映画を見ました。

note.ja: sub（下の）+ title（題）。「副題」→ 画面の下の文字 →「字幕」。

en: Belonging or relating to the branch of Islam based on the Qur'an, the Kutub al-Sittah (the hadiths which record the Sunnah) and that plac…
A follower of Sunni Islam.

Sunni.ety: From Arabic سُنِّيّ (sunniyy), from سُنَّة (sunna, “Sunna”) + ـِيّ (-iyy). By surface analysis, Sunna + -i.

ex.en: Most Muslims in the country are Sunni.
ex.ja: その国のイスラム教徒の大半はスンニ派だ。

note.ja: アラビア語 sunna（慣行・規範）から。「スンニ派」。

en: The condition of tasting sugary or tasting as if sugary, from either sugar or another sweet-tasting substance.
A pleasant disposition; kindness.

sweetness.ety: From Middle English swetnes, swetnesse, from Old English swētnes (“sweetness”), from Proto-West Germanic *swōtinassī (“sweetness”), equivalent to sweet + -ness. Cognate with West Frisian swietens (“sweetness”), obsolete Dutch zoetenis (“sweetness”), Old High German swuoznessi, suoznessi (“sweetness”).

ex.en: The sweetness of the fruit surprised me.
ex.ja: その果物の甘さに驚いた。

note.ja: sweet（甘い）+ -ness。「甘さ・優しさ」。

en: The cooperative effort of a team of people to achieve a common goal.

teamwork.ety: From team + work. Compare West Frisian teamwurk (“teamwork”).

ex.en: The most wonderful thing about baseball is teamwork.
ex.ja: 野球の最もすばらしいところはチームワークだ。

ex.en: Each muscle shows perfect teamwork.
ex.ja: それぞれの筋肉が完璧なチームワークを示す。

ex.en: Teamwork is important in soccer.
ex.ja: サッカーは連携が大切だ。

note.ja: team（チーム）+ work（仕事）。「チームワーク」。

en: An alcoholic liquor distilled from the fermented juice of the Central American century plant Agave tequilana.

tequila.ety: Borrowed from Mexican Spanish tequila, from Tequila, a town in Jalisco.

ex.en: I can't drink tequila.
ex.ja: テキーラは飲めないんだ。

ex.en: Tom is drinking tequila.
ex.ja: トムはテキーラを飲んでいる。

ex.en: Tequila mixed with hot water also has a beautiful taste, it seems.
ex.ja: テキーラのお湯割りも美味しいらしい。

note.ja: メキシコの町テキーラ（Tequila）から。そこで作られた蒸留酒。

en: A ground-dwelling plant.
Of or relating to the Earth or its (native) inhabitants.
Of, relating to, or composed of land or earth, as contrasted with bodies of water, with wetlands viewed as semiaquatic environs, or with …

terrestrial.ety: From Middle English terrestrialle, from terrestre or Latin terrestris, from terra (“land, earth, ground”), with the suffix -al.

note.ja: dangerous（危険な）+ -ly。「危険なほど」。

en: To criticize or speak out against (someone or something); to point out as deserving of reprehension, etc.; to openly accuse or condemn in…
To make a formal or public accusation against; to inform against; to accuse.

denounce.ety: From Old French denuncier, from Latin dēnūntiō (“to announce, to denounce, to threaten”), from de + nūntiō (“to announce, to report, to denounce”), from nūntius (“messenger, message”). Doublet of denunciate.

ex.en: White was denounced to the police as a spy.
ex.ja: ホワイトはスパイだとして警察に告発された。

ex.en: She denounced him to the police as a murderer.
ex.ja: 彼女は彼を人殺しとして警察に訴えた。

ex.en: He was denounced as a coward.
ex.ja: 彼は卑怯者だと非難された。

note.ja: ラテン語 denuntiare ＝ de + nuntiare（告げる）。「公然と告げる」→「公然と非難する」。announce と同じ。

en: That has had something added in order to dilute it.

ex.en: The milk was diluted with water.
ex.ja: 牛乳には水が混ぜてあった。

note.ja: dilute（薄める）+ -ed。di（離して）+ luere（洗う）。「洗い流して薄める」。

en: A current of air or water running back, or in an opposite direction to the main current.
A circular current; a whirlpool.
To form an eddy; to move in, or as if in, an eddy; to move in a circle.

eddy.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *éti
Proto-Germanic *idi-
Proto-West Germanic *id-
Old English ed-
Proto-Indo-European *h₂ékʷeh₂
Proto-Germanic *ahwō
Proto-West Germanic *ahu
Old English ēa
Old English edēa
Middle English eddy
English eddy
From Middle English eddy, from Old English edēa, from ed- (“turning, back, reverse”) + ēa (“water”), equivalent to ed- + ea. Ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₁é, and, consequently, cognate with Latin et. Related also to Danish ide (“eddy”), Swedish eda (“eddy”), Norwegian ida, ia, ea (“eddy”), Icelandic iða (“eddy”).

ex.en: Leaves spun around in an eddy of the stream.
ex.ja: 木の葉が小川の渦の中でくるくる回った。

note.ja: 北欧語 iða（渦）から。「渦」。

en: Evading capture, comprehension or remembrance.
Difficult to make precise.

elusive.ety: From Latin elusus, past participle of eludo (“to parry a blow, to deceive”).

ex.en: Success remained elusive for the young team.
ex.ja: その若いチームにとって、成功はなかなかつかめなかった。

note.ja: elude（逃れる）+ -sive。e（外へ）+ ludere（遊ぶ）。「巧みに逃れる」→「とらえどころのない」。illusion と同じ lud。

en: The act or process of learning secret information through clandestine means.

espionage.ety: Recorded since 1793, from French espionnage, from espionner (“to spy”), from Middle French espionner (“to spy”), from espion (“spy”), from Old French espion (“spy”), from Frankish *spehō (“spy”), from Frankish *spehōn (“to spy”), from Proto-Germanic *spehōną (“to spy, peek, peer”). In modern times, the French pronunciation of the s, which had fallen silent since the 13th century, was restored due to the influence of Italian spione (“spy”), and was therefore also adopted by the English. More at spy.

ex.en: A brilliant, seductive chef turns to espionage in Napoleon-era France.
ex.ja: ナポレオン時代のフランス、卓越した才能で魅了するシェフがスパイに転じる。

note.ja: フランス語 espionnage から。espion（スパイ）。spy と同じ語源。

zh: 有關存在的 /有关存在的
存在主義的 /存在主义的

en: Of or relating to existence.
Concerning the very existence of something, especially with regard to evading extinction.

existential.ety: The adjective is a learned borrowing from Late Latin existentiālis, exsistentiālis (“coming into or relating to existence”) + English -al (suffix meaning ‘of or pertaining to’ forming adjectives; and forming nouns of verbal action). Existentiālis, exsistentiālis are derived from Late Latin existentia, exsistentia (“existence”) + Latin -ālis (suffix forming adjectives of relationship); and existentia, exsistentia from Latin existēns, exsistēns (“being, existing; appearing, emerging; becoming”) (the present active participle of existō, exsistō (“to be, exist; to appear, emerge; to become”), from

ex.en: Climate change is an existential threat to many species.
ex.ja: 気候変動は多くの種にとって存続にかかわる脅威だ。

note.ja: existence（存在）+ -ial。「存在に関わる・実存的な」。existential threat（存亡に関わる脅威）。

en: The act of experimenting; practice by experiment.
A set of actions and observations, performed to verify or falsify a hypothesis or to research a causal relationship between phenomena.

experimentation.ety: From Latin ex- + -periri (akin to periculum), "attempt". Morphologically experiment + -ation.

ex.en: Observation is a passive science, experimentation an active science.
ex.ja: 観察は消極的な科学であり、実験は積極的な科学である。

note.ja: experiment（実験）+ -ation。ラテン語 experiri（試す）。「実験・試行」。expert と同じ。

zh: 極端主義者 /极端主义者

en: A person who holds extreme views, especially one who advocates such views; a radical or fanatic.
Holding extreme views, especially on a political or religious subject.
Of or relating to extremism.

extremist.ety:
Etymology tree
English extreme
Proto-Indo-European *-id-
Proto-Indo-European *-yéti
Proto-Indo-European *-idyéti
Proto-Hellenic *-íd͏̌d͏̌ō
Ancient Greek -ῐ́ζω (-ĭ́zō)
Proto-Hellenic *-tās
Ancient Greek -τής (-tḗs)
Ancient Greek -ῐστής (-ĭstḗs)bor.
Latin -istader.
Old French -istebor.
Middle English -ist
English -ist
English extremist
From extreme + -ist.

ex.en: Tom is an extremist.
ex.ja: トムは過激な思想の持ち主だ。

note.ja: extreme（極端な）+ -ist。ラテン語 extremus（いちばん外の）。「過激派」。

en: A dramatic device in which an earlier event is inserted into the normal chronological flow of a narrative.
A vivid mental image of a past trauma or other sensation that the trauma is happening in the present, especially one that recurs.
To undergo a flashback; to experience a vivid mental image from the past.

ex.en: The movie tells her childhood in a series of flashbacks.
ex.ja: その映画は彼女の子ども時代を一連の回想場面で描いている。

note.ja: flash（ぱっと光る）+ back（後ろへ）。「過去の場面がぱっとよみがえること」。

en: A motion like that of waves; a moving in this and that direction; an irregular rising and falling.
A wavering; unsteadiness.

fluctuation.ety: Borrowed from Latin fluctuatiōnem, accusative singular of fluctuatiō, from fluctuō, from fluctus. Morphologically fluctuate + -ion.

ex.en: There was a sudden fluctuation in temperature.
ex.ja: 気温が急に変動した。

note.ja: fluctuate（変動する）+ -ion。ラテン語 fluctus（波）、fluere（流れる）。「波のように上下すること」→「変動」。fluid と同じ flu。

en: A utensil in the shape of an inverted hollow cone terminating in a narrow pipe, for channeling liquids or granular material; typically us…
A passage or avenue for a fluid or flowing substance; specifically, a smoke flue or pipe; the chimney of a steamship or the like.
To use a funnel.
To proceed through a narrow gap or passageway akin to a funnel; to condense or narrow.

funnel.ety:
From Middle English funell, fonel, probably through Old French *founel (compare Middle French fonel, Old Occitan fonilh, enfounilh), from Latin fundibulum, infundibulum (“funnel”), from infundere (“to pour in”);
in (“in”) + fundere (“to pour”); compare Breton founilh (“funnel”), Welsh ffynel (“air hole, chimney”). See fuse.

ex.en: Use a funnel to pour the oil into the bottle.
ex.ja: じょうごを使って油を瓶に注いでください。

note.ja: ラテン語 infundibulum（じょうご）から。fundere（注ぐ）。「じょうご」→「注ぎ込む」。fuse と同じ fund。

en: A surface shine or luster.
A superficially or deceptively attractive appearance.
To give a gloss or sheen to.
To make (something) attractive by deception

gloss.ety: Probably from a North Germanic language, compare Icelandic glossi (“spark, flame”), glossa (“to flame”); or perhaps from dialectal Dutch gloos (“a glow, flare”), related to West Frisian gloeze (“a glow”), Middle Low German glȫsen (“to smoulder, glow”), German glosen (“to smoulder”); ultimately from Proto-Germanic *glus- (“to glow, shine”), from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰel- (“to flourish; be green or yellow”). More at glow.

ex.en: The furniture has a beautiful gloss.
ex.ja: その家具には美しい光沢がある。

note.ja: 「光沢」は北欧語に由来する。「注釈」はギリシャ語 glōssa（舌・言葉）からで別語。glossary（用語集）。

en: A small shoot or scion of a tree inserted in another tree, the stock of which is to support and nourish it. The two unite and become one …
A branch or portion of a tree growing from such a shoot.
To insert (a graft) in a branch or stem of another tree; to propagate by insertion in another stock; also, to insert a graft upon.
To insert scions (grafts) from one tree, or kind of tree, etc., into another; to practice grafting.

graft.ety: From Middle English graffe, from Old French greffe (“stylus”), from Latin graphium (“stylus”), from Ancient Greek γραφείον (grapheíon), from γράφειν (gráphein, “to write”); probably akin to English carve. So named from the resemblance of a scion or shoot to a pointed pencil. Doublet of graphium. Compare graphic, grammar.

ex.en: The orchardist grafted an apple bud onto the rootstock.
ex.ja: 果樹栽培者がリンゴの接ぎ穂を台木に接ぎ木しました。

ex.en: Select the graft point after imagining how the branches will extend and fruit grow.
ex.ja: 枝が伸び、実が成ることを想定して接ぐ場所を選びましょう。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 graphion（尖筆）から。尖筆の形をした接ぎ穂 →「接ぎ木・移植片」。「汚職」は別系統とされる。

en: Dissatisfied and irritable.
A dissatisfied and irritable person.

grumpy.ety:
Etymology tree
English grump
Proto-Indo-European *-kos
Proto-Germanic *-gaz
Proto-West Germanic *-g
Old English -iġ
Middle English -y
English -y
English grumpy
From grump + -y.

ex.en: Why does he look grumpy?
ex.ja: なぜ彼は不機嫌な顔をしてるんだい。

ex.en: Jane has been quiet and grumpy for the past few days.
ex.ja: ここ数日間、ジェーンは口も利かず不機嫌だ。

ex.en: I'm feeling really grumpy. I guess it's PMS.
ex.ja: なんかすごいイライラする。生理前だからかな。

note.ja: grump（不平）+ -y。擬音的な語。「不機嫌な」。

en: A customary way of speaking or acting; a fashion, a manner, a practice (often used formerly in such phrases as "at his own guise"; that i…
An external appearance in manner or dress; an appropriate indication or expression; a garb; a shape.

guise.ety: From Middle English guise, gise, gyse, from Old French guisse, guise, vise (“guise, manner, way”), from Old Frankish *wīsa (“manner, way, fashion”), from Proto-Germanic *wīsǭ (“manner, way”), from Proto-Indo-European *weyd- (“to see, view, behold, perceive”). Cognate with Old High German wīsa (“way, manner”), Old English wīse (“way, manner”), Dutch wijze (“way, manner”). More at wise.

ex.en: He visited the house in the guise of a salesman.
ex.ja: 彼はセールスマンを装ってその家を訪れた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 guise（やり方・外見）から。wise（方法：otherwise）と同じ祖先。「見せかけ」。disguise と同じ。

en: Increased in intensity or concentration; elevated.

ex.en: There is heightened security at the airport today.
ex.ja: 今日は空港の警備が強化されている。

note.ja: heighten（高める）+ -ed。height と同じ。「高まった」。

en: To become quiet.
To make quiet.
A silence, especially after some noise.

hush.ety: From Middle English huschen (“to hush”) (as past participle husht (“silent; hushed”) and interjection husht (“quiet!”)). Cognate with Low German huschen, hüssen (“to hush; lull”), German huschen (“to shoo; scurry”), Danish hysse (“to hush”), and maybe Albanian hesht.

ex.en: She got into the room with hushed steps.
ex.ja: 彼女は足音を殺して部屋に入った。

ex.en: She hushed her baby to sleep.
ex.ja: 彼女は赤ん坊をあやして眠らせた。

note.ja: 擬音語。「シーッ」→「静かにさせる・静けさ」。

en: The act of imitating.
A copy or simulation; something that is not the real thing.

imitation.ety: From Middle English imitacioun, from Middle French imitacion, from Old French imitacion, from Latin imitatio.

ex.en: He compared the imitation with the original.
ex.ja: 彼はその模造品を本物と比較した。

ex.en: I don't care for imitation.
ex.ja: 私は模造品は好まない。

ex.en: This is an imitation diamond.
ex.ja: これは模造ダイヤモンドです。

note.ja: imitate（まねる）+ -ion。ラテン語 imitari（まねる）。image と同系。「模倣・模造品」。

en: The total submerging of a person in water as an act of baptism.
Deep engagement in something.

immersion.ety: From late Middle English, borrowed from Late Latin immersiō, immersiōnem (“dipping”).

ex.en: Language immersion is a great way to learn.
ex.ja: その言語にどっぷり浸かることは、すばらしい学習方法だ。

note.ja: immerse（浸す）+ -sion。in + mergere（浸す）。「浸すこと」→「没頭」→ 言語の「イマージョン教育」。

en: not convenient

inconvenient.ety: Borrowed from Middle French inconvenient, from Latin inconvenientem.

ex.en: It is inconvenient to work in evening clothes.
ex.ja: 夜会服は仕事をするには不便だ。

ex.en: If our quote is inconvenient for you, please let us know.
ex.ja: 私どもの見積書に対してご質問がありましたら、至急ご連絡ください。

ex.en: If there were no telephones, it would be inconvenient.
ex.ja: もし電話がなければ、不便だろう。

note.ja: in（否定）+ con（共に）+ veni（来る）+ ent。うまく合わない →「不便な・都合の悪い」。

ex.en: The employees were intrigued by the odd behavior of their boss.
ex.ja: 従業員はボスの奇行に困っていた。

note.ja: intrigue（興味をそそる）+ -ed。イタリア語 intrigare（もつれさせる）。「興味をそそられた」。

en: Innate, inherent, inseparable from the thing itself, essential.
Situated, produced, secreted in, or coming from inside an organ, tissue, muscle or member.
A built-in function that is implemented directly by the compiler, without any intermediate call to a library.
An ability possessed by a character and not requiring any external equipment.

intrinsic.ety: From Middle French intrinsèque, from Latin intrīnsecus (“on the inside, inwardly”), from *intrim, an assumed adverbial form of inter (“within”) + secus (“by, on the side”).

ex.en: Music has intrinsic value beyond money.
ex.ja: 音楽にはお金では測れない本質的な価値がある。

note.ja: ラテン語 intrinsecus（内側に）から。「本質的な・固有の」。extrinsic（外的な）と対。

en: Impossible to resist.
Compellingly attractive.

irresistible.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *né
Proto-Indo-European *n̥-
Proto-Italic *n̥-
Latin in-
Proto-Italic *wre-
Latin re-
Proto-Indo-European *steh₂-
Proto-Indo-European *stísteh₂ti
Proto-Italic *sistō
Latin sistō
Latin resisto
Proto-Indo-European *-dʰlom
Proto-Italic *-ðlom
Proto-Italic *-ðlis
Latin -bilis
Latin irresistibilislbor.
English irresistible
Learned borrowing from Medieval Latin irresistibilis, equivalent to ir- + resistible.

ex.en: The Dodgers went on winning with irresistible force.
ex.ja: ドジャースは破竹の勢いで勝ち進んだ。

ex.en: The urge to brag on his recent successes was irresistible.
ex.ja: 彼は先ごろの成功を自慢したくてたまらない。

note.ja: ir（否定）+ re（逆らって）+ sist（立つ）+ ible。逆らって立つことができない →「抵抗できない・たまらなく魅力的な」。

en: A natural disaster that involves the breakup and downhill flow of rock, mud, water and anything caught in the path.
A vote won by a wide or overwhelming majority.
To undergo a landslide.

landslide.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *lendʰ-
Proto-Indo-European *-om
Proto-Germanic *landą
Proto-West Germanic *land
Old English land
Middle English lond
English land
Proto-Indo-European *h₃sleydʰ-
Proto-Indo-European *-eti

Proto-Germanic *slīdaną
Proto-West Germanic *slīdan
Old English slīdan
Middle English sliden
English slide
English landslide
From land + slide.

ex.en: That landslide produced a lot of misery.
ex.ja: あの地滑り事故は多くの不幸を生んだ。

ex.en: Traffic was blocked by a landslide.
ex.ja: がけくずれで交通は遮断された。

note.ja: land（土地）+ slide（すべること）。「地滑り」→ 票が雪崩を打つ →「圧勝」。

en: A strap, cord or rope with which to restrain an animal, often a dog.
A string with a loop at the end for lifting warp threads, in a loom.
To fasten or secure with a leash.
to curb, restrain

leash.ety: From Middle English leesshe, leysche, lesshe, a variant of more original lease, from Middle English lees, leese, leece, lese, from Old French lesse (modern French laisse), either from Latin laxa, feminine form of laxus (“loose”) or, more probably, from a deverbal of Old French lesser, laissier, from Latin laxāre (“loose”); compare lax. Doublet of laisse.

ex.en: Tom keeps Mary on a short leash.
ex.ja: トムはメアリーを束縛してるんだ。

ex.en: As soon as I let go of the leash, the dog ran away.
ex.ja: 綱を離すと犬は走り去った。

note.ja: 古フランス語 laisse（ゆるめた綱）から。ラテン語 laxus（ゆるい）。relax と同じ。「引き綱」。

en: A major change in the use of something, or in the appearance of something or someone; a radical transformation.

ex.en: Maybe it's time to change my hair and do a makeover.
ex.ja: そろそろ髪型でも変えて、イメチェンしようかな。

note.ja: make over（作り直す）の名詞化。「イメージチェンジ・改装」。

en: A short note serving as a reminder.
A written business communication.

memorandum.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin memorandum, neuter of memorandus (“to be remembered”).

ex.en: This is a memorandum.
ex.ja: これは備忘録です。

note.ja: ラテン語で「覚えておくべきこと」。memorare（思い出させる）。memo の元の形。

en: A mythological creature with a woman's head and upper body, and a tail of a fish.
Coloured a brilliant turquoise.

mermaid.ety: From Middle English mermayde (“maid of the sea”), from mere (“sea, lake”) + maid, equivalent to mer- + maid. Cognate with Dutch meermeid (“mermaid”), Middle High German mermaget, mermeit (“mermaid”, > German Meermagd, Meermädchen (“mermaid”)). Compare Old English meremenn, meremennen, meremenin (“mermaid, siren”).

ex.en: The legend says that she was a mermaid.
ex.ja: 伝説では、彼女は人魚だったと言われる。

note.ja: mere（海）+ maid（乙女）。「海の乙女」→「人魚」。marine と同じ祖先。

en: The state or quality of being moderate; avoidance of extremes.
An instance of moderating: bringing something away from extremes, especially in a beneficial way.

moderation.ety:
Etymology tree
Latin *med-der.?
Latin *-osder.?
Latin moderō
Proto-Indo-European *-tis
Proto-Indo-European *-Hō
Proto-Indo-European *-tiHō
Proto-Italic *-tiō
Latin -tiō
Latin moderātiō
Old French moderacion
Middle French [Term?]bor.
English moderation
Borrowed from Middle French [Term?], from Old French moderacion, from Latin moderātiō. By surface analysis, moderate + ion.

ex.en: It's all right to drink, but drink in moderation.
ex.ja: 酒もいいが大概にしておきなさい。

ex.en: It's best to drink in moderation.
ex.ja: 酒は飲んでも飲まれるな。

ex.en: It's better to drink in moderation.
ex.ja: 飲酒を控えたほうがいいです。

note.ja: moderate（適度な）+ -ion。ラテン語 modus（尺度）。「節度・司会」。mode、modest と同じ mod。

en: A person from Morocco.
Of, from, or pertaining to Morocco or the Moroccan people.

ex.en: We drank sweet Moroccan mint tea.
ex.ja: 私たちは甘いモロッコのミントティーを飲んだ。

note.ja: Morocco + -an。都市マラケシュ（Marrakesh）の名から。

en: A noble or privileged social class, historically accompanied by a hereditary title; aristocracy.
The quality of being noble.

nobility.ety: From Old French nobilité, from Latin nobilitas. Equivalent to noble + -ity.

ex.en: The palace was built for the nobility.
ex.ja: その宮殿は貴族のために建てられた。

note.ja: noble（高貴な）+ -ity。ラテン語 nobilis（知られた・高貴な）、noscere（知る）。「貴族・高潔さ」。notice と同じ。

en: The act, process, method, or an instance of representing by a system or set of marks, signs, figures, or characters.
A system of characters, symbols, or abbreviated expressions used in an art or science or in mathematics or logic to express technical fac…

notation.ety: From Latin notātiō, equivalent to notate + -ion or note + -ation.

ex.en: Musical notation can be hard to read at first.
ex.ja: 楽譜の記号は最初は読むのが難しいことがある。

note.ja: ラテン語 notatio（印をつけること）から。nota（印）。「表記法」。note と同じ。

en: On the part of a stage that is visible to the audience.
Taking place on the part of a stage that is visible to the audience.

ex.en: The actor was onstage for most of the play.
ex.ja: その男優は劇の間中ほとんど舞台上にいた。

note.ja: on + stage（舞台）。「舞台上の」。

en: A trial in which the accused was subjected to a dangerous test (such as ducking in water), divine authority deciding the guilt of the acc…
A painful or trying experience.

ordeal.ety:
From Middle English ordel, ordal, from Medieval Latin ordālium or inherited from its source Old English ordēl, ordāl (“ordeal, judgement”), from Proto-West Germanic *uʀdailī (“judgement”, literally “an out-dealing”), from *uʀdailijan (“to deal out; dispense”). For more, see Old English or-, English deal.
Cognate with Saterland Frisian Uurdeel (“judgement; verdict”), West Frisian oardiel (“judgement”), Dutch oordeel (“judgement, discretion”), Low German Oordeel (“judgement; verdict”), German Urteil (“judgement, verdict”).

ex.en: Bob has to get through this ordeal on his own.
ex.ja: ボブは自分の力でこの厳しい試練を乗り切らねばいけない。

note.ja: 古英語 ordāl（神明裁判）から。苦痛に耐えられれば無実とする裁判 →「試練」。

en: An adult castrated male of cattle (B. taurus), especially when used as a beast of burden.
Any bovine animal (genus Bos).

ox.ety:
From Middle English oxe, from Old English oxa, from Proto-West Germanic *ohsō, from Proto-Germanic *uhsô (compare West Frisian okse, Dutch os, German Ochse), from Proto-Indo-European *uksḗn.
Cognate with Welsh ych (“ox”), Tocharian A ops, Tocharian B okso (“draft-ox”), Avestan 𐬎𐬑𐬱𐬀𐬥 (uxšan, “bull”), Sanskrit उ॒क्षन् (ukṣán).

ex.en: He that will steal an egg will steal an ox.
ex.ja: 卵を盗む奴は牛も盗む。

ex.en: He who steals a pin will steal an ox.
ex.ja: 一事が万事。

ex.en: Yoke the oxen to the plow.
ex.ja: 牛にくびきをかけすきにつなぎなさい。

en: In a painful manner; as if in pain.
Badly; poorly.

ex.ja: 彼は痛ましいほどやせていた。

ex.en: Tom was painfully thin.
ex.ja: トムは痛々しいほどに痩せていた。

ex.en: The sudden glare impinged painfully on his eyes.
ex.ja: 突然の強い光を受けて彼の目は痛いほどだった。

note.ja: painful + -ly。「痛いほど・ひどく」。

en: Of events, experiences, or phenomena, that cannot be explained by current scientific understanding or natural laws.
Paranormal phenomena collectively: all things paranormal; things with paranormality.
A person to whom paranormal powers are attributed.

paranormal.ety: From para- (“beyond”) + normal; compare supernatural. First use appears c. 1905.

ex.ja: アメリカ人の4分の3が超常現象を信じている。

note.ja: para（超えた）+ normal（ふつうの）。「超常的な」。

en: An edible fruit produced by the pear tree, similar to an apple but typically elongated towards the stem.
A type of fruit tree (Pyrus communis).

ex.ja: 箱の中には梨がいくつかある。

ex.ja: この梨は、最後に食べよっと。

ex.ja: 僕は梨を無料でもらった。

note.ja: ラテン語 pirum から。「洋ナシ」。

en: A solid disk or cylinder that fits inside a hollow cylinder, and moves under pressure (as in an engine) or displaces fluid (as in a pump)
A valve device in some brass instruments for changing the pitch
To move up and down or in and out like a piston.

ex.en: This shaft links with a piston.
ex.ja: このシャフトはピストンとつながっている。

note.ja: イタリア語 pistone（大きなすりこぎ）から。pestare（突く）。pestle（すりこぎ）と同じ。

en: In a polite manner.

ex.ja: もっと丁寧な話し方をすべきだったのに。

note.ja: polite（丁寧な）+ -ly。ラテン語 politus（磨かれた）。polish と同じ語源。

en: A fine, granular substance produced in flowers.
Pollen grains (microspores) produced in the anthers of flowering plants.
To cover with, or as if with, pollen.

pollen.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin pollen (“fine flour”), used by Carl Linnaeus in the 18th century to describe the spores produced in the anthers of flowers.

ex.ja: 私は花粉アレルギーだ。

ex.ja: トムは花粉症がある。

note.ja: ラテン語 pollen（細かい粉）から。「花粉」。powder と同系。

en: A developmental phase brought about by the action of hormones as part of the maturing process. For humans, there are three in total.
The process of sexual development that produces secondary sex characteristics and makes a person capable of reproducing sexually.

puberty.ety: From Middle English puberte, from Old French puberté, from Latin pūbertās (“the age of maturity, manhood”).

ex.en: Children's voices often change during puberty.
ex.ja: 子どもの声は思春期に変わることが多い。

note.ja: ラテン語 pubertas（成人）から。pubes（成人・陰毛）。「思春期」。

en: A music genre that originated in Jamaica in the late 1960s and is heavily associated with Rastafarianism, featuring a heavy bass line and…

reggae.ety: From Jamaican Creole rege (“rags; a quarrel”), see rag; originally used in the 1960s to describe a Jamaican dance. Compare ragtime. Broader musical sense popularized by the 1968 Maytals song “Do the Reggay”.

ex.en: What do you think of reggae?
ex.ja: レゲエのことをどう思いますか。

ex.en: What do you think about reggae?
ex.ja: レゲエってどう思う？

note.ja: ジャマイカの言葉。語源ははっきりしない。

ex.ja: そのチームは２部に降格した。

note.ja: relegate（格下げする）+ -ed。re + legare（送る）。「追い払う」→「降格した」。

ex.ja: 彼は目上の人に対して丁重である。

The act of thinking again about something.

ex.ja: パイプをくわえたその紳士は有名な評論家です。

en: The act of writing again or anew.
Something that has been written again.
To write again, differently; to modify; to revise.
To write again (without changes).

en: A gathering of cattle to be branded.
A North American sport involving skills with horses, cows and other livestock.
To perform in a rodeo show.

rodeo.ety: From Spanish rodeo, from rodear (“to surround”), which refers to a cattle roundup.

ex.ja: カウボーイたちがロデオで競い合った。

note.ja: スペイン語 rodeo（家畜の駆り集め）から。rodear（囲む）、ラテン語 rota（車輪）。「ロデオ」。rotate と同じ rot。

en: An administrative area or district between about the 5th to the 11th century, subdivided into hundreds or wapentakes and jointly governed…
The people living in a shire (noun sense 1.1) considered collectively.
To constitute or reconstitute (a country or region) into one or more shires (noun sense 1.1) or counties.

shire.ety:
The noun is derived from Middle English schire (“region, shire, county”) [and other forms], from Old English sċīr (“administrative region under an alderman and sheriff, shire; district under a governor or official; status of an official, office”) [and other forms], from Proto-West Germanic *skīru (“district; status of an official, office”); further etymology uncertain, possibly related to Latin cūra (“care, concern; administration, charge, management; command, office”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kʷeys- (“to heed; to see”).
The verb is derived from the noun.

ex.en: He lives in a quiet village in the shire.
ex.ja: 彼はその州の静かな村に住んでいる。

note.ja: 古英語 scīr（行政区）から。Yorkshire などの -shire。sheriff（shire reeve：州の役人）と同じ。

en: A narrow cut or opening; a slot.
To cut a narrow opening.
To split into strips by lengthwise cuts.
Having a cut narrow opening.

slit.ety: From Middle English slitten, from Old English slītan, from Proto-Germanic *slītaną (“to tear apart”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)leyd- (“to tear, rend (cut apart), split apart”). Possibly cognate with Latin laed- (“to strike, hurt, injure”). Doublet of slite; also related to slice through French borrowing. Apparently unrelated to English slot, whose etymology, however, is uncertain.

ex.en: My eyes narrowed into slits in the strong sunlight.
ex.ja: 私の目は強い日光を浴びて細くなった。

note.ja: 古英語 slītan（裂く）から。slice と同系。「細長い切れ目」。

en: Act of one who sobs; a crying or weeping.
That or who sobs.

ex.en: I could hear her sobbing in her bedroom.
ex.ja: 彼女が部屋ですすり泣くのが聞こえた。

ex.en: I found that there was a little girl sobbing.
ex.ja: 一人の小さな女の子がしくしく泣いているのをみつけた。

ex.en: On entering the bedroom, she started sobbing.
ex.ja: 寝室に入るや否や、彼女は泣きじゃくり出した。

note.ja: sob（すすり泣く）+ -ing。擬音的な語。

en: An inhibition or ban that results from social custom or emotional aversion.
Something which may not be used, approached or mentioned because it is sacred.
Excluded or forbidden from use, approach or mention.
Culturally forbidden.
To mark as taboo.
To ban or prohibit.

taboo.ety:
Borrowed from Tongan tapu (“prohibited, sacred”), from Proto-Polynesian *tapu, from Proto-Oceanic *tabu, from Proto-Eastern Malayo-Polynesian *tambu. Doublet of kapu. First attested in c. 1777.
The p in the Tongan source was misheard as b.

ex.ja: かつて女性の喫煙はタブー視されていた。

ex.en: The excessive use of salt should be taboo.
ex.ja: 塩を過剰に使うのは避けるべきだ。

ex.en: The topic is taboo here.
ex.ja: その話はここではタブーです。

note.ja: トンガ語 tabu（神聖で触れてはいけない）から。キャプテン・クックが英語に伝えた。

A person or thing that teases.

en: A valve that regulates the supply of fuel-air mixture to an internal combustion engine and thus controls its speed; a similar valve that …

To control or adjust the speed of (an engine).
To cut back on the speed of (an engine, person, organization, network connection, etc.).

throttle.ety: From Middle English *throtel, diminutive of throte (“throat”), equivalent to throat + -le. Compare German Drossel (“throttle”). More at throat.

ex.ja: パイロットはスロットルを前に押した。

A quiz game that involves obscure facts.

ex.ja: 尾羽打ち枯らした彼の姿を見るのは忍びないね。

ex.ja: 耐えられない圧迫から逃れるために自殺に走る子供たちもいる。

ex.ja: 非暴力主義者のマハトラ・ガンジーは１８６９年に生まれた。

Extremely unfavorable; terrible.

ex.ja: 環境破壊は驚くほどすすんでいる。

ex.en: She is an appalling cook.
ex.ja: 彼女は料理が恐ろしく下手だ。

ex.en: She's an appalling cook.
ex.ja: 彼女は料理が恐ろしく下手だ。

note.ja: appall（ぞっとさせる）+ -ing。古フランス語 apalir（青ざめる）、pale（青白い）と同じ。「ぞっとするような」。

en: To express approval (of something) by clapping the hands.
To praise, or express approval for something or someone.

applaud.ety: From Middle English applauden, from Latin applaudere (“to clap the hands together, applaud”), from ad (“to”) + plaudere (“to strike, clap”).

ex.en: The audience applauded for a full five minutes.
ex.ja: 観客はたっぷりと５分間拍手した。

ex.en: The large audience applauded when the song finished.
ex.ja: 大勢の客は歌が終わると拍手をした。

ex.en: I applaud your decision to study medicine.
ex.ja: 医学を勉強しようという君の決心に私は拍手を送る。

note.ja: ap（〜へ）+ plaud（拍手する）。〜に拍手する →「拍手を送る・称賛する」。applause（拍手）。

en: Of a person, who has been subjected to the rite of baptism.

ex.en: And people were constantly coming to be baptized.
ex.ja: 人々は、次々にやってきてバプテスマを受けていた。

ex.en: He was baptized a Catholic.
ex.ja: 彼は洗礼を受けてカトリック教徒となった。

ex.en: She was baptized Mary.
ex.ja: 彼女はメアリーと名付けられた。

note.ja: baptize（洗礼を施す）+ -ed。ギリシャ語 baptizein（水に浸す）。

en: The state of being enslaved or the practice of slavery.
The state of lacking freedom; constraint.

bondage.ety: Inherited from Middle English bondage (“serfdom”), from British Medieval Latin bondagium (“an inferior tenure held by a bond or husbandman”), from Middle English bond (“tenant farmer, serf”), from Old English bonda (“householder, husband, head of a family”), of Old Norse origin. Sense development influenced by the unrelated terms bond and bind.

ex.en: I guess she's into bondage and domination.
ex.ja: 彼女のフェチが緊縛と支配でしょう。

ex.en: He liberated the people from bondage.
ex.ja: 彼は人々を束縛から解放した。

note.ja: bond（縛るもの）+ -age。「束縛・隷属」。bind と同じ。

en: The state of being bored.
An instance or period of being bored; a bored state.

ex.en: One will come to find boredom in anything no matter what.
ex.ja: 何にだって飽きは来る。

ex.en: Autistic children don't know what boredom is.
ex.ja: 自閉症の子供は飽きることを知らない。

ex.en: The boredom is unbearable.
ex.ja: 私は退屈でかなわない。

note.ja: bored（退屈した）+ -dom。「退屈」。kingdom、freedom と同じ -dom。

en: In a brilliant manner; with brilliance.

brilliantly.ety:
Etymology tree
English brilliant
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English brilliantly
From brilliant + -ly.

ex.en: Quasars are brilliantly shining heavenly bodies that are extremely far away.
ex.ja: クエーサーとは、非常に遠方にある、まぶしい輝きを放つ天体だ。

note.ja: brilliant + -ly。「見事に」。

ja: ブランチ（朝昼兼用の食事）

en: A meal eaten later in the day than breakfast and earlier than lunch, often in a leisurely, festive, and/or social way, and often consisti…
To eat brunch.

brunch.ety: Blend of breakfast + lunch. Attested from 1895 in British English and from 1930 in the United States.

ex.en: We had brunch at a café on Sunday.
ex.ja: 日曜日に私たちはカフェでブランチを食べた。

note.ja: breakfast + lunch を合わせた語。

en: An edible nut (technically a fruit) of the Spanish chestnut or sweet chestnut tree (Castanea sativa); also (chiefly preceded by a descrip…
In full chestnut tree: the shrub or tree that bears this nut, the Spanish chestnut or sweet chestnut (Castanea sativa); also (chiefly pre…
Of a deep reddish-brown colour, like that of a chestnut fruit (noun sense 1).

chestnut.ety:
The noun is a contraction of chest(en) (“(obsolete) chestnut tree; fruit of this tree, chestnut”) + nut. Chesten is a late variant of chesteine (obsolete), from Middle English chesten, chesteine, chasteine, chesteyne (“chestnut tree (Castanea sativa); fruit of this tree; wood of this tree”), from Old French chastaigne, chastaine (French châtaigne), from Latin castanea (“chestnut tree; fruit of this tree”) (whence Old English ċisten), from Ancient Greek κᾰστᾰ́νειᾰ (kăstắneiă), a variant of κᾰ́στᾰνᾰ (kắstănă, “sweet chestnut”); for further etymology, see that entry. Doublet of castanet.
Noun sen

ex.en: Mom, I want some chestnut rice. Can you make some?
ex.ja: お母さん、栗ご飯食べたいから、栗ご飯作って。

ex.en: The chestnut horse is fast.
ex.ja: この栗毛馬、速いなぁ。

ex.en: Ouch! A chestnut fell on my head.
ex.ja: 痛っ！栗が頭に落ちてきた。

note.ja: 古英語 chesten（クリ）+ nut。ギリシャ語 kastanea。「クリ・栗色」。

en: A professional laundry or dry cleaner.

ex.en: I have to take my suit to the cleaners.
ex.ja: スーツをクリーニングに出さなきゃ。

ex.en: I need to take my suit to the dry cleaners.
ex.ja: スーツをクリーニングに出さなきゃ。

ex.en: Cats hate vacuum cleaners.
ex.ja: ネコは掃除機が大嫌い。

note.ja: cleaner（清掃員）の複数形。the cleaners（クリーニング店）。

en: The act of cleaning or tidying something.
The act of finishing something off.

ex.en: Tom bats cleanup on our team.
ex.ja: 我がチームではトムが４番を打つ。

note.ja: clean up（片づける）の名詞化。「掃除・浄化」。

en: Brief, yet including all important information.
To make concise; to abridge or summarize.

concise.ety: From Latin concīsus (“cut short”), from concīdere (“cut to pieces”), from caedēre (“to cut, to strike down”).

ex.en: His comment was concise and to the point.
ex.ja: 彼の評論は簡潔で要点を押さえたものだった。

ex.en: His address is a concise speech.
ex.ja: 彼の演説は簡潔スピーチです。

ex.en: I need a concise explanation.
ex.ja: 簡潔な説明をしてほしい。

note.ja: con（完全に）+ cis（切る）+ e。すっかり切り詰めた →「簡潔な」。precise（正確な）、decide（決める）も同じ caedere。

en: The act of confining or the state of being confined.
lockdown

confinement.ety: Borrowed from French confinement. By surface analysis, confine + -ment.

ex.en: The prisoner spent years in confinement.
ex.ja: その囚人は何年も監禁されていた。

note.ja: confine（閉じ込める）+ -ment。con + finis（境界）。「監禁」。

en: A consultant or consulting firm.
The services offered by a consultant.

ex.en: She runs a small marketing consultancy.
ex.ja: 彼女は小さなマーケティングのコンサルタント会社を経営している。

note.ja: consultant + -cy。「コンサルタント会社」。

en: An act of incurring debt; also (generally), an act of acquiring something (generally negative).
The process of contracting or becoming infected with a disease.

contraction.ety:
PIE word
 *ḱóm
From Late Middle English contraccioun, contraxion (“spasm, contraction; constriction, shrinking; act of pressing together”), from Old French contraction (modern French contraction), from Latin contractiō(n) (“a drawing together, contraction; abridgement, shortening; dejection, despondency”), from contrahō (“to draw things together, assemble, collect, gather; to enter into a contract”) + -tiō(n) (suffix forming nouns relating to actions or their results). Contrahō is derived from con- (prefix denoting a bringing together of objects) + trahō (“to drag, pull”) (probably from Proto-

ex.en: How far apart are the contractions?
ex.ja: 陣痛の間隔はどれくらいですか。

ex.en: My contractions last about forty-five seconds.
ex.ja: 陣痛が約４５秒続きます。

note.ja: con（共に）+ tract（引く）+ ion。引き縮めること →「収縮・短縮形（I'm など）」。

en: The act of moving toward union or uniformity.
A meeting place.

ex.en: The city stands at the convergence of two rivers.
ex.ja: その都市は二つの川が合流する地点にある。

note.ja: converge（集まる）+ -ence。con + vergere（傾く）。「1点に向かうこと」→「収束」。diverge（分かれる）と対。

en: That which is deducted; that which is subtracted or removed.
A sum that can be removed in tax calculations, usually from the taxable amount; something that is written off.

deduction.ety:
From Middle French déduction, from Latin deductio.
Equivalent to deduct + -ion or deduce + -tion.

ex.en: The tax agent allowed the deduction.
ex.ja: 税務署は控除を認めた。

ex.en: Luxury spending is ineligible for tax deductions.
ex.ja: 贅沢への支出は税控除の対象とはならない。

ex.en: An income tax is levied on any income that exceeds deductions.
ex.ja: 所得税は控除額を上回るいかなる所得にもかかる。

note.ja: de（下へ・離れて）+ duct（導く）+ ion。引き下ろすこと →「控除・差し引き」、結論を導き出すこと →「演繹」。

en: Fit or deserving to be despised; contemptible; mean.
A wretched or wicked person.

despicable.ety: From Late Latin dēspicābilis, from Latin dēspicor, a variant of dēspiciō (“to despise”), from de (“down”) + speciō (“to look at, behold”). First attested in the 1550s. Equivalent to despise + -able.

ex.en: Everyone saw through his despicable schemes.
ex.ja: あいつの卑劣なたくらみをみんな見透かしていた。

ex.en: I am ashamed of your despicable deed.
ex.ja: きみの言語道断な行いを恥ずかしいと思う。

note.ja: de（下へ）+ spic（見る）+ able。見下されるべき →「卑劣な・見下げ果てた」。despise（軽蔑する）。

en: The action of detaching; separation.
The state of being detached or disconnected; insulation.

detachment.ety: From French détachement. By surface analysis, detach + -ment.

ex.en: I had retinal detachment five years ago.
ex.ja: ５年前に網膜剥離を起こしました。

ex.en: Detachment provides perspective, which in turn permits a certain amount of pattern recognition.
ex.ja: 離れることで全体が見渡せるようになり、今度はそれで、ある程度のパターン認識ができるようになるのである。

note.ja: detach（引き離す）+ -ment。de（離して）+ attach。「分離・無関心・分遣隊」。

en: Of, relating to, or functioning in digestion.
That causes or promotes digestion.
A substance that aids digestion.
A digestive biscuit.

digestive.ety: From Old French digestif, from Late Latin dīgestīvus. Doublet of digestif.

ex.en: The digestive system breaks down food.
ex.ja: 消化器系は食べ物を分解する。

note.ja: di（ばらばらに）+ gest（運ぶ）+ ive。消化（digest）の →「消化の」。

en: To make smaller.
To become less or smaller.

diminish.ety: Formed under the influence of both diminue (from Old French diminuer, from Latin dīminuo) and minish.

ex.en: To say so should not diminish his importance.
ex.ja: そう言ったからといって彼の重要性が低下するわけではない。

ex.en: The population of this country is diminishing.
ex.ja: この国の人口はだんだん減っている。

ex.en: The deficit has been diminishing little by little.
ex.ja: 赤字は徐々に減少している。

note.ja: ラテン語 deminuere（小さくする）から。de + minuere（減らす）。「減る・減らす」。minus、minor と同じ min。

en: One who disclaims, disowns, or renounces.
A public disavowal, as of responsibility, pretensions, claims, opinions, etc.
To disclaim or disavow, as by appending a legal disclaimer.

disclaimer.ety: Partly from Middle English discleymer, from Anglo-Norman desclamer; and partly from disclaim + -er.

ex.en: Read the disclaimer before you use the website.
ex.ja: ウェブサイトを使う前に免責事項を読んでください。

note.ja: disclaim（否認する）+ -er。dis + claim（主張する）。「権利を主張しないという宣言」→「免責事項」。

en: To sever or interrupt a connection.
To remove the connection between an appliance and an electrical power source.
A break or interruption in an existing connection, continuum, or process; disconnection.
A switch used to isolate a portion of an electrical circuit.

en: Causing disruption or unrest.
Causing major change, as in a market.

disruptive.ety: From disrupt + -ive. In the business sense popularized by Clayton Christensen and Joseph Bower, see 1995 citation.

ex.en: Lately that student has been disruptive in class. Honestly it's beginning to worry me.
ex.ja: その子最近授業中遊び倒しているので、正直今後が心配。

note.ja: disrupt（混乱させる）+ -ive。dis + rumpere（壊す）。「破壊的な」→ 既存市場を覆す「破壊的（イノベーション）」。rupture と同じ rupt。

en: In an endless manner; continuously without limit.

endlessly.ety: From Middle English endelesly, from Old English endelēaslīċe; equivalent to endless + -ly.

ex.en: The schoolboys teased each other endlessly.
ex.ja: 男子学生たちはひっきりなしにふざけあっていた。

ex.en: Mr. Koizumi talks endlessly without stopping.
ex.ja: 小泉さんは話の切れ目のない人です。

ex.en: The song I heard before in the train station loops endlessly around my head.
ex.ja: さっき駅で聴いた曲が頭の中をエンドレスで回っている。

note.ja: endless（果てしない）+ -ly。「果てしなく」。

en: A medical condition in which the sufferer experiences seizures (or convulsions) and blackouts.

epilepsy.ety: Since 16th century; borrowed from French épilepsie, from Latin epilēpsia, from Ancient Greek ἐπιληψίᾱ (epilēpsíā), from ἐπιλαμβάνω (epilambánō, “to seize”), from ἐπι- (epi-, “upon”) + λαμβάνω (lambánō, “to take”). Displaced native Old English fiellesēocnes (literally “falling sickness”).

ex.en: People with epilepsy can usually live normal lives.
ex.ja: てんかんのある人も、たいていはふつうの生活を送ることができる。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 epilēpsis（捕らえられること）から。epi（上に）+ lambanein（つかむ）。「（発作に）つかまれること」→「てんかん」。

en: The process of making an estimate.
The amount, extent, position, size, or value reached in an estimate.

estimation.ety: From Middle English estimacioun, estimacion, from Old French estimacion, from Latin aestimatio. Morphologically estimate + -ion.

ex.en: In my estimation, he is an honest man.
ex.ja: 私の見たところでは彼は正直者です。

ex.en: Your estimation of him is a little high, to say the least.
ex.ja: 君の彼に対する評価は、ひかえ目に言っても、少し高いよ。

ex.en: You must not base your estimation of a person on rumor alone.
ex.ja: うわさだけに基づいて人の評価をしてはならない。

note.ja: estimate（見積もる）+ -ion。ラテン語 aestimare（値をつける）。「見積もり・評価」。esteem と同じ。

en: The act of excavating, or of making hollow, by cutting, scooping, or digging out a part of a solid mass.
Especially, the trade of digging engineered holes for building foundations, roadbed preparations, and similar purposes.

excavation.ety: From Latin excavātiō (“a hollowing out”), from excavō (“to hollow out”), from ex + cavō (“to hollow out”), from cavus (“hollow”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḱewh₁- (“vault, hole”). Equivalent to excavate + -ion.

ex.ja: 発掘で古代の墓が見つかった。

note.ja: excavate（発掘する）+ -ion。ex（外へ）+ cavare（くり抜く）。「発掘」。cave と同じ。

en: A battery-powered hand-held light source.
A flashgun (device used to create flashes of light for photography).
To illuminate with a flashlight.

ex.en: We would now like to have some sample flashlights.
ex.ja: ライトの実物を検討させていただきたいと思います。

ex.en: Can you please send ten $15 flashlights immediately?
ex.ja: 単価１５ドルで１０本を至急送っていただけますか。

ex.en: I shone a flashlight into the dark room.
ex.ja: 暗い部屋の中を懐中電灯で照らした。

note.ja: flash（ぱっと光る）+ light（明かり）。「懐中電灯」。

en: Attractive or good-looking; that makes one look good.
Gratifying to one's self-esteem; complimentary.
The action of the verb to flatter.
Instances of flattery.

flattering.ety: From Middle English flatering, flatrung (gerund), equivalent to flatter + -ing.

ex.en: That color is very flattering on you.
ex.ja: その色はあなたにとてもよく似合う。

note.ja: flatter（お世辞を言う）+ -ing。古フランス語 flater（なでる）。「お世辞の」→ 実物より「よく見せる」。

en: In a forcible manner, by force, against one's will.
In a forcible manner, with force, with powerful effect, powerfully, strongly.

forcibly.ety: From Middle English forceably, equivalent to forcible + -ly.

ex.en: The rioters were forcibly removed from the plaza.
ex.ja: 暴徒は広場から強制的に排除された。

note.ja: forcible（強制的な）+ -ly。force（力）。「強制的に」。

en: A circular or linear decoration, especially one of plaited flowers or leaves, worn on the body or draped as a decoration.
An accolade or mark of honour.
To deck or ornament something with a garland.
To form something into a garland.

garland.ety:
From Middle English garland, garlaunde, gerland, from Old French garlande, garlaunde, gerlande, guerlande (compare French guirlande), from Frankish *wierlōn, *wieralōn, a frequentative form of Frankish *wierōn (“to adorn, bedeck”), from *wiera (“a gold thread”), from or related to Proto-Germanic *wīraz.

ex.en: The children wore garlands of flowers.
ex.ja: 子どもたちは花輪を身に着けていた。

note.ja: 古フランス語 garlande（花輪）から。「花輪」。

en: The Holy Grail.
Something eagerly sought or quested for.

grail.ety: From Middle English graal, greal, from Old French graal, greal (“cup”), from Medieval Latin gradalis, possibly corrupted over time from Latin crater (“bowl”).

ex.en: Finding a cure is the holy grail of cancer research.
ex.ja: 治療法を見つけることは、がん研究の究極の目標だ。

en: Innovative; new, different; doing something that has never been done before.
The point at which construction begins, by digging into the ground.
A ceremony to mark the beginning of construction.

groundbreaking.ety: From ground + breaking, in reference to the practice of breaking ground at the beginning of a new building or construction.

ex.ja: 当時としちゃ画期的な発明だったね。

note.ja: ground（地面）+ breaking（掘る）。「起工の」→「画期的な」。

en: The state or condition of being holy.

holiness.ety: From Middle English holynesse, holinesse, halinesse, from Old English hāliġnes (“holiness, a holy thing, rites”), from Proto-West Germanic *hailagnassī, equivalent to holy + -ness. Cognate with West Frisian hilligens (“holiness”), Old High German heilagnissi, heilīgnissi (“holiness”), whence Middle High German heilignis (“halidom”).

ex.en: His Holiness the Pope visited Japan.
ex.ja: ローマ教皇聖下が日本を訪問した。

note.ja: holy（神聖な）+ -ness。「神聖さ」。holy は whole（完全な）と同じ祖先。

en: Tending to inspire horror; that horrifies; horrific.

ex.en: The debate has been interesting, confusing, and sometimes horrifying.
ex.ja: ここでの討論はおもしろいものでしたし、困惑させるもの、ときにはぞっとする内容のものもありました。

note.ja: horrify + -ing。「ぞっとする」。horror と同じ。

en: Liable to humiliate, degrade, shame or embarrass someone.
An act of humiliation.

ex.en: Losing ten to nothing was humiliating.
ex.ja: １０対０で負けたのは屈辱的だった。

note.ja: humiliate（恥をかかせる）+ -ing。ラテン語 humilis（低い）。「屈辱的な」。humble と同じ。

ex.ja: 貿易不均衡が大きな問題であるように思える。

en: To show to be connected or involved in an unfavorable or criminal way.
To imply without entailing; to have as an implicature.
The thing implied.

implicate.ety: First attested in the 15th century, in Middle English; inherited from Middle English implicaten (poorly attested), from implicat(e) (“wrapped, entwined; involved, connected (with)”, possibly also used as the past participle of implicaten) + -en (verb-forming suffix), borrowed from Latin implicātus, perfect passive participle of implicō (“to entangle, involve”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from plicō (“to fold”). Doublet of imply and employ.

ex.en: The evidence implicated the manager in the crime.
ex.ja: その証拠から、支配人がその犯罪に関わっていたことが分かった。

note.ja: ラテン語 implicare ＝ in + plicare（折る）。「折り込む」→「巻き込む・関与させる」。imply、implication と同じ plic。

en: Not efficient; not producing the effect intended or desired; inefficacious.
Incapable of, or indisposed to, effective action; habitually slack or unproductive; effecting little or nothing.

ex.ja: 古い暖房設備はとても効率が悪い。

note.ja: in（否定）+ efficient（効率的な）。「非効率な」。

en: To render more intense.
To become intense, or more intense; to act with increasing power or energy.

ex.en: The storm is expected to intensify tonight.
ex.ja: 今夜、嵐が強まると予想されている。

note.ja: in（中へ）+ tens（伸ばす）+ ify。ぴんと張りつめさせる →「強める・激化する」。

en: The state of being intolerant.
Extreme sensitivity to a food or drug; of a food that is generally considered edible, an individual inability to digest it.

intolerance.ety: Borrowed from French intolérance, itself from in- (“not”) + tolérance or borrowed from Latin intolerantia (“insolence, insufferableness; (very rare) intolerance”). By surface analysis, in- + tolerance.

ex.en: Our topic of the week is intolerance.
ex.ja: 今週の話題は「不寛容さ」についてです。

note.ja: in（否定）+ tolerance（寛容）。「不寛容・不耐性」。

en: A member of a jury.

juror.ety: From Middle English jurour, jurrour, borrowed from Anglo-Norman jurour and Old French jureor, from the verb jurer (“to swear”), or possibly from Latin iūrātor, iūrātōrem, whence the English doublet jurator.

ex.en: Each juror listened carefully to the evidence.
ex.ja: 陪審員はそれぞれ証拠に注意深く耳を傾けた。

note.ja: jur（誓う）+ or（人）。誓いを立てた人 →「陪審員」。jury（陪審）。

en: The tenth letter of the Greek alphabet.
A measurement of the sensitivity of the value of an option to changes in the implied volatility of the price of the underlying asset.

kappa.ety: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek κάππα (káppa), ultimately from Proto-Semitic *kapp- (“palm, hand”). Doublet of kaph.

ex.en: In Japanese folklore, a kappa lives in rivers.
ex.ja: 日本の民間伝承では、河童は川に住んでいる。

note.ja: ギリシャ文字 κ。日本語の「河童」も英語で kappa と書かれる。

ex.ja: ケチャップ、買い忘れた。

en: Any of a class of types of cancer affecting the blood cells, especially the white blood cells (usually with massive leukocytosis), and th…

leukemia.ety: From German Leukämie, from Ancient Greek λευκός (leukós, “white”) + αἷμα (haîma, “blood”). By surface analysis, leuk- + -emia.

ex.en: Tom was diagnosed with leukemia.
ex.ja: トムは白血病と診断されました。

ex.en: He died from acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
ex.ja: 彼は急性リンパ性白血病で死亡しました。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 leukos（白い）+ haima（血）。「白い血」→「白血病」。

en: Descent in a line from a common progenitor; progeny; descending line of offspring or ascending line of parentage.
A number of lines of text in a column.

lineage.ety: From Middle English linage, from Old French linage, from ligne, from Latin linea (“line”); equivalent to line + -age.

ex.en: The family can trace its lineage back to the 12th century.
ex.ja: その一家は家系を１２世紀までさかのぼることができる。

note.ja: 古フランス語 lignage（家系）から。ラテン語 linea（線）。「血統」。line と同じ。

en: The total number of all available workers; the workforce.
The power exerted by a single person.

ex.en: Is there enough manpower in the kitchen?
ex.ja: 厨房って、人が足りてる？

ex.en: Adding manpower to a late software project makes it later.
ex.ja: 遅れているソフトウェアプロジェクトに人員を追加するとさらに遅れる。

ex.en: "Manpower" is the world's largest temp agency.
ex.ja: マンパワーは世界で一番大きな人材派遣会社です。

note.ja: man（人）+ power（力）。「人手」。

To make someone into a martyr by putting them to death for adhering to, or acting in accordance with, some belief, especially religious; …
To persecute.

martyr.ety: From Middle English martir, from Old English martyr, itself a borrowing from Ecclesiastical Latin martyr, from Ancient Greek μάρτυρ (mártur), later form of μάρτυς (mártus, “witness”).

ex.en: He was honored as a martyr for his faith.
ex.ja: 彼は信仰に殉じた人としてたたえられた。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 martys（証人）から。信仰の証人として死ぬ人 →「殉教者」。

en: Sexual stimulation of one's genitalia or other erotic regions, often to the point of orgasm.
The stimulation of another person's genitals using the hands.

masturbation.ety: Borrowed from French masturbation, New Latin masturbātiō, masturbātiōnem. By surface analysis, masturbat(e) + -ion.

ex.ja: オナニーは狂気につながる。

note.ja: ラテン語 masturbari から。語源ははっきりしない。

en: A reduction or decrease of something harmful or unpleasant.

mitigation.ety: From Middle French mitigation, from Latin mītigātiō.

ex.ja: 洪水被害の軽減は市の最優先課題だ。

note.ja: mitigate（和らげる）+ -ion。ラテン語 mitis（穏やかな）+ agere（する）。「緩和」。

ex.ja: 私たちはジャンクション１１で高速道路を出た。

ex.ja: 高速道路が渋滞している。

note.ja: motor（自動車）+ way（道）。「（英）高速道路」。

en: Offensive to standards of decency or morality.
Lewd or lustful.

obscene.ety:

The further etymology is uncertain, but may be from ob- (prefix meaning ‘towards’) + caenum (“dirt, filth; mire, mud”) (possibly ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱweyn- (“to make dirty, soil; filth; mud”)) or scaevus (“left, on the left side; clumsy; (figurative) unlucky”) (from Proto-Indo-European *skeh₂iwo-). ex.en: Or are there photographs so obscene that you can't publish them?
ex.ja: それとも、あまりに猥褻な写真があるから出版できないということか？

note.ja: ラテン語 obscenus（不吉な・汚らわしい）から。「わいせつな」。

en: A person who occupies an office or a position.
A person who occupies a place.

occupant.ety: Borrowed from Middle French occupant (present participle of occuper) or Latin occupāns, occupantis (present participle of occupō). By surface analysis, occupy + -ant.

ex.en: The occupants of the car were not hurt.
ex.ja: その車の乗員はけがをしなかった。

note.ja: occupy（占める）+ -ant。「居住者・乗員」。

To spread out in long arms or legs in many directions.

ex.ja: 昔々、タコたちは地上をうろついていました。

In a forward direction.

To form by striking with the beak or a pointed instrument.
An act of striking with a beak.
A small kiss.

ex.ja: 鳥たちが地面をつついている。
